title: Trowers & Hamlins partners with Legora after pilot reaches 97% adoption
author: Legora

dom.t: Legora partnerships: Adoption needs selected workflows and training

st.t: Legora partnerships: Adoption needs selected workflows and training
st.an: The source supports the platform-led adoption narrative with a broader rollout following live-workflow testing, while reinforcing the synthesis’s qualifications: its strongest evidence concerns usage and participant ratings rather than independently measured productivity, accuracy or client outcomes, and it preserves lawyer review and AI governance as conditions of responsible deployment.
qs: The results were decisive:  97% of participants reported using Legora weekly  88% rated quality “good” or “excellent”  87% found it “easy” or “very easy” to use  These findings confirmed strong adoption, broad usability, and meaningful value for lawyers across practice areas.
Trowers & Hamlins’ approach ensures that AI-generated results are carefully reviewed, refined, and contextualised by skilled practitioners.

kp.k: Pilot-reported adoption and usability precede firm rollout
kp.d: Legora’s October 2, 2025 newsroom announcement reports that Trowers & Hamlins has begun rolling out its platform across legal departments after lawyers tested it in live workflows. Among pilot participants, 97% reported weekly use, 88% rated quality “good” or “excellent”, and 87% found it “easy” or “very easy” to use. These are reported participant usage and ratings; the announcement does not specify the participant count or pilot duration.
qs: International law firm Trowers & Hamlins has begun rolling out Legora across its legal departments, following a successful pilot programme.
97% of participants reported using Legora weekly
87% found it “easy” or “very easy” to use

kp.k: Lawyer input and governance shaped live-workflow testing
kp.d: The announcement describes a pilot led jointly by the firm’s Innovation and Legal Technology team and AI Governance Group. Lawyers’ aspirations and concerns shaped testing scenarios, while experimentation and feedback were intended both to assess the platform and strengthen understanding of responsible integration into practice.
qs: The pilot was led by Trowers & Hamlins’ Innovation and Legal Technology team, working alongside the firm’s AI Governance Group.
From the outset, lawyers were invited to share aspirations and concerns, helping to shape the scenarios against which Legora was tested.

By creating a supportive environment for experimentation and feedback, the programme not only assessed Legora’s capabilities but also strengthened understanding of how AI can be integrated responsibly into practice.

kp.k: Firm representative reports practical uses across practice areas
kp.d: In a customer quotation carried by Legora, Rob Mallett, the firm’s Innovation and Legal Technology Operations Manager, says the pilot validated numerous valuable, practical use cases across practice areas. He identifies quality, ease of use and adoption as reasons for selecting Legora, but does not identify particular tasks or quantify time savings or client outcomes.
qs: It's quality, ease of use and strong adoption confirmed that Legora is the right tool for us as we take the next step on our AI journey.
During the pilot phase, we validated a large number of highly valuable and practical use cases spanning a wide range of our practice areas.

kp.k: Lawyers retain project leadership and verify AI outputs
kp.d: Partner and innovation champion Victoria Robertson describes an augmentation approach: lawyers continue steering legal projects and review, refine and contextualise AI-generated results. She states that an implemented AI governance framework, overseen by the firm’s AI Governance Group, supports safe adoption aligned with professional standards. These are the firm representative’s statements about its approach, rather than independently measured findings about output reliability.
qs: Whilst we are embracing technology to enhance the work we do for our clients, this partnership does not diminish the vital role that lawyers play in steering every legal project.
Trowers & Hamlins’ approach ensures that AI-generated results are carefully reviewed, refined, and contextualised by skilled practitioners.

To support this, we've implemented a robust AI governance framework, overseen by our AI Governance Group, to ensure that our adoption of AI is safe, responsible, and aligned with our professional standards.

kp.k: Vendor frames AI as amplification rather than replacement
kp.d: Legora presents the partnership as reflecting a shared belief that AI should amplify legal expertise rather than replace it. CEO Max Junestrand says the pilot gave the vendor insights into supporting lawyers’ daily work and highlighted responsible innovation. This expresses the partnership’s intended model of legal work, not evidence of changes in lawyer headcount or staffing structures.
qs: For Legora, this partnership reflects both firms’ shared belief that AI should amplify, not replace, legal expertise.
Their thorough pilot programme gave us invaluable insights into how Legora can support lawyers in their daily work, while also highlighting the importance of responsible innovation.

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: Legora presents the pilot as demonstrating adoption and practical value across practice areas, and frames the rollout as supporting more efficient, precise and collaborative legal work.
pts.d: The Legora newsroom article reports that Trowers & Hamlins has begun deploying its product across legal departments after a pilot in live workflows. It interprets participants’ reported use, quality ratings and usability ratings as confirming meaningful value. Rob Mallett, the firm's Innovation and Legal Technology Operations Manager, separately says the pilot validated numerous practical use cases across practice areas. The article's broader claims about efficiency, precision and collaboration are qualitative benefits asserted for the rollout, rather than quantified pilot outcomes.

pts.k: The partnership is explicitly framed as augmenting lawyers rather than replacing their expertise, with lawyers continuing to direct projects and verify AI outputs.
pts.d: Legora describes augmentation as the partners’ shared belief. Victoria Robertson, a Trowers & Hamlins partner and innovation champion, says lawyers retain a vital steering role and review, refine and contextualise AI-generated results. She attributes the maintenance of professional standards to human oversight and the firm's governance framework. This is a human-in-the-loop model of legal work, not a prediction of autonomous legal delivery or evidence about future lawyer headcount.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The evidence offered consists of participant-reported pilot metrics, experience testing live workflows and testimonials from firm personnel and Legora's CEO.
pts.d: The vendor-authored announcement reports weekly use by 97% of participants, good or excellent quality ratings from 88%, and easy or very easy usability ratings from 87%. These are adoption and subjective assessment measures, not objective accuracy, time-saving or client-outcome measurements. The document does not specify participant numbers, pilot duration, task-level results or a comparison group. Mallett supplies experiential support through his account of validated use cases. Legora CEO Max Junestrand says the pilot yielded insights into supporting lawyers’ daily work; no separate quantitative evidence is supplied for the broader efficiency, precision or collaboration claims.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: The pilot precedes an underway rollout as of 2 October 2025; the claimed benefits are tied to careful implementation, governance and continuing human oversight.
pts.d: The announcement is dated 2 October 2025. Mallett describes pilot planning as beginning 'late last year', implying late 2024, but no exact pilot dates or rollout completion deadline are given. Pilot findings concern participants’ use during the trial, while wider benefits are presented as the direction of the ongoing rollout. The article conditions AI's role as a trusted aid on rigour, transparency and human oversight. Robertson identifies an implemented governance framework overseen by the AI Governance Group as supporting safe adoption aligned with professional standards.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The immediate affected groups are Trowers & Hamlins lawyers across practice areas, the firm's innovation and governance teams, and clients receiving lawyer-supervised services.
pts.d: Lawyers at the international law firm are the direct users, with AI intended to support daily workflows while leaving professional direction and output verification with practitioners. The Innovation and Legal Technology team and AI Governance Group lead testing and responsible implementation. Clients are described as beneficiaries of enhanced legal work and maintained professional standards, without reported client-outcome measurements. Legora is the software provider and says it gained insights from the pilot. The source does not make claims about displacement, pricing, access to justice or market-wide employment effects.
